records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: ww A 40 year old female presents to ED complaining of complete visual loss in her right eye. On fundoscopy you note a pale retina and a cherry red spot. You suspect an emboli. Which of the following blood vessels is most likely the source of the emboli:
options: Anterior cerebral artery (x) Middl cerebral artery 8%
Posterior cerebral artery (Vv) Internal carotid artery 56%
records.explanation: The internal carotid artery is the most likely source of the emboli. The ophthalmic artery arises from the internal carotid artery and supplies structures in the orbit and eyeball. The central retinal artery is the most important branch of the ophthalmic artery, supplying the retina and the optic disc. The central retinal artery is an end artery that does not anastomose with other arteries, and thus its occlusion results in monocular blindness. : Vv

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: ww A 65 year old lady presents to ED complaining of sudden onset visual loss. On examination you demonstrate visual loss on the right side of the vertical midline with macular sparing in both eyes. Which of the following blood vessels is most likely occluded:
records.explanation: The posterior cerebral artery supplies blood to the visual cortex in the occipital lobe. A lesion to this area will result in a contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing. . Vv Arterial Supply of Brain

She is placed on the stroke pathway. Which of the following blood vessels has most likely been occluded:
options: Anterior cerebral artery (x) Posterior cerebral artery 4%
records.explanation: The anterior cerebral artery supplies the medial cerebral hemisphere including the paracentral lobule which is formed from portions of the frontal and parietal lobes, and responsible for the motor and sensory function of the lower limb. v
